question: DEF setup on Lotus C Site, round start, you are Cypher. Where do you place your Trapwire to cover the rotating B-C door and the C split?

options.label: Place the Trapwire on the C access path through the door but OUTSIDE the door rotation radius so it survives the turn
options.explication_courte: The rotating door destroys any util deployed inside its rotation radius; placing the Trapwire just outside that radius covers the split entry while surviving the mechanic.

options.label: Place the Trapwire deeper inside C Site on a secondary angle far from the door
options.explication_courte: A deep site trap survives and gives late info, but it misses the B-C door split entry window that is the most dangerous rotation path on C.

sources_option.citation: A deep site trap survives but gives only late info; the rotating-door split is a primary C entry that should be covered closer to the choke.

options.label: Place the Trapwire directly in the door opening to block the split as early as possible
options.explication_courte: Placing the trap inside the rotation radius seems to cover the split earliest, but the moment the door rotates, it destroys your trap - zero coverage at the critical moment.

sources_option.citation: Never park deployable utility in a door's rotation path; anything sitting there gets destroyed the instant it spins — Cypher Trapwire and Cyber Cage are the most commonly lost.

options.label: Skip the Trapwire entirely and save all util for a retake later
options.explication_courte: Not placing any info on C leaves you blind on the smallest and most easily overwhelmed site on the map; early warning is Cypher's highest-value contribution on C.

sources_option.citation: C Site is one of the smallest sites with four entry points; leaving it without early information gives attackers an easy overwhelm, wasting a sentinel's info role.

explication_longue:
Situation: DEF setup on Lotus C Site, round start, you are Cypher with Trapwire, Cyber Cage, Spycam. The question is where to place the Trapwire to cover the rotating B-C door and the C split.

Lotus has a unique mechanic: its rotating doors destroy any utility deployed inside their rotation radius the moment they spin. This is the defining Cypher placement constraint on C Site. The correct placement is just outside the rotation radius of the B-C door, on the corridor connecting to C - this covers the split entry path after the door passes without the door destroying the wire.

Deeper site placement (acceptable) survives and provides later info, but misses the earliest warning opportunity on the most dangerous rotation vector. Placing inside the rotation radius (costly) seems correct but the door destroys it at rotation - zero coverage when it matters most. Skipping the Trapwire (mistake) blinds you entirely on C, the smallest site with the fewest defensive angles and the highest speed-of-execute risk.

Estimated elite distribution: ~55% outside rotation radius on C access, ~22% deeper site trap, ~15% inside rotation radius (costly), ~6% no trap (mistake).

sources.citation: Never park deployable utility anywhere in a door's rotation path, as anything sitting in the path gets destroyed the instant it spins; Killjoy Alarmbot, Cypher Trapwire/Cyber Cage and Sage Slow Orb are the most commonly lost.
The rotating door at C is a key rotation path; Cypher Trapwire or Killjoy utility near the door catches attackers using it for a split — placed clear of the rotation arc.
C Site is arguably the smallest site in the game with very few holding spots but four entry points, making early access information especially valuable.
